@ImJustCray @traciemac_Bmore Because there is too much going on. That's how this can work.

There was so much excellent investigative journalism going on with #MeToo.  Most of it!  There was an assumption by people that this was more of that, but it simply was not.

@KD0571 @lauferlaw I wrote multiple times as well.

He wanted to stay, and he knows how to fight (though navigating through #MeToo made it really challenging, but he was trying). And then, Gillibrand jumped in and made his staying untenable. It was horrible.

@takingaction4us @voxdotcom @alfranken @washingtonpost @MsIngaSpoke @Smartypants60 @mtomasky Article also suggests only men raising issue. But I know there are many women who feel same way. Perhaps older women, not sure, with longer perspective / experience but also plenty of #MeToo women who are furious at even equivalence (even assuming guilt, which I don’t).

@JohnMashey @AmyJBrittain @irin @JulieATate @alice_crites @shanesnow Cool.  Shane did cover a lot of the important factors (I know, you are hitting same ones as well).  I thought his going into touchy aspect of "told this to friends through the years" was particularly good.  This matters, of course, in corroboration of many #MeToo stories. 1/?

@bmoschetti @chrislhayes I have no idea the proportions -- I see both, people who adamantly think she was a #MeToo champion and people who think she was an opportunist who denied him the investigation he desired (and said would clear him).

I know I want facts; whatever they are, we haven't gotten them.
